1.

The present claim petition arises out of road accident that occurred on 06.10.2021,
in which one Ashish Kumar (aged about 29 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 06.10.2021 at about 01:00 PM, Sh. Ashish Kumar along with his father Sh. Gitesh Kumar (since deceased) was going to Sampaul Bazar on Scooty bearing no. BR-50H-7091.

When they reached NH-57, Simrahi Bazar,
West Gandhi Nagar, a Scorpio car bearing no.BR-07- Ashish Kumar vs Arvind Thakur on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106006432/
1 PC-4342 (hereinafter referred to the offending vehicle) came at a very high speed driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the scooty of the victim.
As an impact of the collision, both were dragged to few meter on the road.
Petitioner Ashish Kumar sustained grievous injuries while his father Gitesh Kumar died on the spot.
Both were removed to Raghopur Hospital where postmortem of Gitesh Kumar was conducted and treatment was provided to petitioner Ashish Kumar.
3. An FIR no.277/21, dated 07.10.2021 was registered u/s 279/337/338/304-A/427 IPC at PS Radhopur, District Supaul.

Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/337/304-A/427 of IPC before concerned criminal court while two separate claim petitions in respect of injury to the petitioner and qua death of Giteh Kumar (MACT no.326/22) were filed before this Tribunal.
4.

As per record, the offending vehicle was driven and owned by respondent no.1 and insured with respondent no. 2.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner is (inadvertently mentioned as petitioners are) entitled to compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?

OPP.
17.
As regards quantum of compensation, petitioner has claimed to have suffered grievous injury.
During his cross examination as PW-1, he alleged to have become unconscious after the accident ill he was taken to Raghopur Referral Hospital.
He has claimed that his MLC was prepared in the hospital and that he remained admitted for two days.
No medical record qua admission or discharge has however been filed by petition.
In fact, Ex.PW1/5 is a hand written document (nor in the prescribed formate of MLC) that bears a stamp of Raghopur Referral Hospital.

Even this document,
shows 'bruises' and opines the injury to by 'simple in nature'.
No medical bills hence been field in support of alleged medical expenses.

Hence, petitioner is only entitled to (i) expenses relating to treatment, which is Nil, in the present case, (ii) Loss of earnings during period of treatment which is also Nil, as no proof filed and (iii) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequences of the injuries which is awarded as Rs.5,000/-.
Further, Insurance company has not raised any statutory defence and as such is liable to pay compensation.
18.
